newsitem.title: UK: London coffee futures hit one-year high.
newsitem.headline: London coffee futures hit one-year high.

text.p: London coffee futures surged in early Tuesday trading with the benchmark July delivery contract hitting a one-year high of $1,835 a tonne on the back of the sharp New York rally on Monday.
By 0907 GMT, the second-month position was traded at $1,829, still a sharp $54 gain on the day.
The London market trades the robusta type of bean, used mainly in the manufacture of soluble, or instant, coffee.

The July contract has risen by more than 51 percent since the start of the year in frenzied buying, powered by soaring New York-traded arabica coffee futures, whose prices have nearly doubled in the same period.

The rally in the U.S. market was re-ignited on Monday by a report from brokerage Merrill Lynch which said coffee prices could reach record highs ahead of new crop shipments this autumn due to on-going supply tightness.

The market will probably continue to be well underpinned ahead of winter in top-grower Brazil. Two severe frosts in 1994, one in June and another in July, damaged the Brazilian crop and sent world prices sky-rocketing.
